t: Paragraph (2) of section 9 of the Act entitled “An Act relating to the policing of the buildings and grounds of the Smithsonian Institution and its constituent bureaus”, approved October 24, 1951 (65 Slat. 634; 40 U.S.C. 193n et seq.) is amended by inserting “(A)” immediately after “held to extend” and by striking out the period at the end thereof and inserting in lieu thereof a comma and the following: “(B) to the line of the face of the south curb of Pennsylvania Avenue Northwest, between Fourth Street and Third Street Northwest, to the line of the face of the west curb of Third Street Northwest, between Pennsylvania Avenue and Madison Drive Northwest, to the line of the face of the north curb of Madison Drive Northwest, between Third Street and Fourth Street Northwest, and to the line of the face of the east curb of Fourth Street Northwest, between Pennsylvania Avenue and Madison Drive Northwest.”

fable.w: This section only amends the geographic boundaries of the Smithsonian buildings and grounds for policing purposes, describing curb lines along Pennsylvania Avenue, Third Street, Madison Drive, and Fourth Street. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object over any federal decision. There is no tempting participation language here; it is a purely technical boundary amendment.

opus.w: This amendment only extends the boundary line of the Smithsonian grounds to certain street curbs for policing purposes. It sets up no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Nothing here brings non-federal actors into a federal decision, so there is no participation.
opus.b: This section only changes the geographic boundaries of the Smithsonian grounds that are covered by the 1951 policing Act. The tempting-but-wrong reading would be to treat any legislative amendment as a procedural action. But the section involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, so nobody outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
